description_full: LuxExperience B.V., through its subsidiary, operates digital platform for the luxury fashion in Germany, the United States, Europe, Middle East, Japan, mainland China, Hong Kong SAR, China, and internationally. The company offers womenswear, menswear, kidswear, fine jewelry, watches, fine jewelry and lifestyle products under the Mytheresa, NET-A-PORTER, MR PORTER, YOOX, and the OUTNET brand name. The company was formerly known as MYT Netherlands Parent B.V. and changed its name to LuxExperience B.V. in May 2025. LuxExperience B.V. was incorporated in 2019 and is based in Munich, Germany.
ceo_bio: Mr. Michael  Kliger | CEO & Chairman of Management Board | Age 58
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $356K ranks in the below the sector median among Consumer Cyclical peers, with revenue growing 17%/yr across its filed history.
financial_summary: LuxExperience B.V. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.6B market cap on $1.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at -2% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 48%.
The company is burning through $36M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at +25.4% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 79× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 87% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 5.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 9% below the high.

prof: ROIC of 2% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.1%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 2.84).
